label: Fires at GO after a1 reached S1 and was rewarded, stronger when belief favours S1.
short_terms: (phase == GO) ;; (phase == GO) * (prev_state != S2) * (prev_reward == 1) ;; (phase == GO) * (prev_state != S2) * np.maximum(belief_lo, 0)
terms: (phase == GO) * last_is("a1 S1 r") ;; (phase == GO) * last_is("a2 S1 r") ;; (phase == GO) * last_is("a1 S1 u") ;; (phase == GO) * belief_lo ;; (phase == GO) * (prev_state == S1) * belief_lo ;; (phase == GO) * last_is("a1 S1 r") * belief_lo ;; (phase == GO) * (tv("state", -2) == S1) * (tv("reward", -2) == 1) ;; (phase == GO) * (prev_state == -1)
explanation: GO-only feature (zero at D1 and D2). Its magnitude is set mainly by the previous trial: large (~4-5) at GO after a1 -> S1 rewarded (residual +2.9), near zero after any S2 outcome or unrewarded trial, intermediate after a2 -> S1 rewarded and on window-first trials. Within these, the observer log-odds that S1 is good (belief_lo) grades it upward. Trial-before reward, belief_cover and trials-since-reversal add little; the 8-term free fit (more last-trial patterns, trial-before terms) gains only ~0.03 over the 3-term short form. Uses observed quantities only.

issues: The recorded short form has no GO-only constant. The timing baseline is fixed and the intercept is global (misses shows a predicted -0.165 at D1/D2), so GO*belief_lo has to stand in for the GO offset. This produces a large systematic error: misses on the recorded short form over-predicts GO after a1 S2 u by -1.84, after a2 S2 u by -1.17, after a1 S2 r by -1.07 and after a1 S1 u by -0.58. That contradicts the explanation's own claim that the feature is near zero after S2 or unrewarded trials.

Adding (phase == GO) as a term fixes most of this. (phase==GO) ;; GO*last_is('a1 S1 r') ;; GO*(prev_state != S2)*(prev_reward==1) scores 0.764 on test, and swapping the belief term to the rectified version below raises it to 0.821. The 0.83 'all observed' ceiling is therefore nearly reached. The explanation's claim that 'some structure is still unexplained' (free fit 0.652) comes from the missing constant, not from missing structure.

The label is too narrow. Window-first trials (prev_state == -1) count as well: when the previous trial was rewarded they fire like the S1-rewarded cases. The a1-versus-a2 split explains less than the label suggests. Once there is a GO constant, last_is('a1 S1 r') adds less than '(prev_state != S2) & rewarded' together with a belief term restricted to those trials.

The belief effect is one-sided. It only helps when rectified (np.maximum(belief_lo, 0)) and restricted to trials whose previous state was not S2: 0.821, against 0.782 for unrectified belief_lo. A global, linear belief_lo is the wrong shape.
Remaining error with the revised form: GO after a2 S1 r is over-predicted by -0.66 (the a1 S1 r vs a2 S1 r gap is only partly captured), and GO after '?' by -0.24. No other cell exceeds 0.2.
